card.name: Words introducing how something is used
card.fires_on: Short linking words like "as", "used" and "for" right after a drug, treatment or method name, where the next words say how or for what it is applied.

modes.label: "used" after a drug class
modes.description: The word "used" follows a drug group name and leads into the purpose, such as "for any indication".
modes.example: suggests that the risk applies to all AEDs<< used>> for any indication.

modes.label: "as" after a treatment or method
modes.description: The word "as" follows a drug or method name and introduces the role or form in which it is applied.
modes.example: in patients receiving ketamine<< as>> part of a treatment plan that utilizes recurrent

modes.label: "for" after the drug
modes.description: The word "for" follows a drug and leads into the person or purpose it is used for.
modes.example: long-term usefulness of the drug<< for>> the individual patient [see Dosage and

card.writes: It seems to push toward words meaning "applied to" or "used for", with a few code-like terms mixed in.
card.plain: It lights up on small words like "as", "used" or "for" that come right after a drug or treatment and say how it is applied.
